newsitem.title: USA: TCI merges newspaper co in $627 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: TCI merges newspaper co in $627 mln deal.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc said Monday that it had entered a pact valued at about $627 million to merge the Kearns-Tribune Corp, the owner of the Salt Lake Tribune, into a new subsidiary.
TCI said it would issue about 52.8 million shares of its common stock in the deal, which it expects to close before the end of the third quarter.
The purchase is the cable giant's first of a print publishing business.

"We see it as a way for us to move into other areas," said TCI spokesman Mike Smith. "This doesn't mean we're going to roll across the country buying other newspapers, but we can experiment in the market, in electronic publishing and whatever other relationships develop between cable and newspaper."
In addition to the Salt Lake Tribune, Kearns owns four other regional newspapers in the Northwest, real estate, and other assets worth about $286 million.
The company also owns 17.9 million shares of Tele-Communications Inc and 6.7 million shares of Liberty Media Group, a TCI subsidiary.
Smith said TCI is buying the voting B shares of its stock and those of Liberty that Kearns owns and issuing 52.8 million, non-voting A shares of its stock.
As part of the deal, Liberty Media will buy the 6.7 million shares of its stock being acquired by TCI, which is part of a previously announced Liberty stock repurchase plan, TCI said.
The deal is subject to regulatory and Kearns-Tribune shareholder approval.
